analysis.title: UBS Cash Trading - Main Themes 5th November
key_insights: Desk reads the US midterm elections as a clearing event: VIX fell 4.5 vol on the day, expectations for material escalation in the Iran conflict are lower, and technical selling had been exhausted going into the event.

Bipartisan commentary on the impact of the Iran war on the midterms (Trump, Vance and Schumer most impactful) moved markets to reprice the odds of an end to the conflict. Brent is now 12% off its week-to-date highs and crude is -1.3% overnight.
Polymarket odds have barely moved in the near term. The most visible shift is for the end of March 2027, where the odds of the US naval blockade being lifted rose to 71% from 64%.

AI unwind is extending into Asia. AI semis/power/winners are -3-6% and neoclouds -8.4% on the risk of more AI regulation and scrutiny. Kospi is -6% and TAIEX -3%, and the desk sees broad-based de-grossing across the APAC AI supply chain.

Nasdaq futures are -1.4% against S&P -0.3%. Qualcomm is -7.2% after hours after guiding Dec quarter EPS below consensus on a broad-based rise in costs. The desk reads this as negative for handset OEMs (MediaTek, AAC).
China is the beneficiary of the post-midterm rotation: HSTECH +5%, H shares +3%, following KWEB +4.5% in the US session.
Cross-asset moves support the de-escalation read: UST 10yr -5bps to 4.85%, the dollar weaker against all G10 majors (yen back below 158), and gold near $4,110 on lower yields and a softer dollar.
Desk view: US markets continue to underperform on a relative basis, provided the change in market assumptions on US/Iran proves correct.

UBS expects the BoE MPC to hike Bank Rate by 25bp to 4.0% today, in line with market pricing. The vote would flip from 7-2 for a hold in September to 7-2 for a hike, with Dhingra and Taylor expected to favour no change. UBS sees some risk of a more hawkish 8-1 split.

European cash flows on Wednesday were balanced (52/48) with participation about 2x the HT YTD average. Industrials were the busiest sector (26% of turnover) and finished better for sale. Banks (15% of turnover) saw broad-based demand across UK, Italian and Spanish names, with hedge funds at 97/3 and long-only at 61/39 better bid.

Tech (15% of turnover) finished better to buy on semis demand despite sector weakness. Energy saw supply as crude faded, and Consumer Staples saw supply in Food & Bev and Personal Care. Discretionary saw demand in luxury, and Healthcare saw demand in pharma.

market_movers.rationale: Shares are -7.2% after hours after Dec quarter EPS guidance came in below consensus on a broad-based rise in costs. The desk reads it as negative for handset OEMs.

sector_views.rationale: AI semis/power/winners are -3-6% and neoclouds -8.4% on the risk of more AI regulation and scrutiny. De-grossing is spreading across the APAC AI supply chain.
China is the beneficiary of the rotation post-midterms, with HSTECH +5%, H shares +3% and KWEB +4.5% in the US session.
Consumer Discretionary outperformed Energy by 11.2% as a function of oil markets. Crude is -1.3% overnight and Brent is 12% off its week-to-date highs. European Energy saw supply in flows.

earnings_insights: Qualcomm (QCOM) guided Dec quarter EPS below consensus on a broad-based rise in costs (guidance vs consensus, reported after the close on 11/4). Shares are -7.2% after hours. The desk reads it as negative for handset OEMs MediaTek and AAC.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yield fell 5bps overnight, supporting the de-escalation read across assets.
UBS expects a hike in line with market pricing. The vote is forecast at 7-2 for a hike, with a risk of 8-1.
The September vote was 7-2 for a hold, so the majority would flip. Dhingra and Taylor are expected to favour no change.
The September vote is the prior reading before today's expected flip to a hike.
Gold is higher on lower yields and a softer dollar.
The yen is stronger as the dollar weakens against all G10 majors.

risk_factors: The desk's view that US markets underperform relies on the change in US/Iran assumptions proving correct.
AI regulation and scrutiny risk is driving the neocloud and semis unwind.
Escalation risk in the Iran conflict could return if the de-escalation read fails.
A more hawkish BoE vote (8-1) is a risk to the UBS base case.
vol_and_positioning: VIX fell 4.5 vol yesterday, which the desk reads as the election acting as a clearing event and a release valve for risk assets.
Technical selling was exhausted going into the election (per earlier desk notes).
Broad-based de-grossing is visible across the APAC AI supply chain.
European cash flows: hedge funds were 97/3 and long-only 61/39, both better bid in banks. Overall flows were balanced at 52/48 with participation about 2x the HT YTD average.
geopolitical: Iran war: the desk says Democratic and Republican speakers both talked about the war's impact on the midterm elections. Trump, Vance and Schumer commentary was the most impactful in repricing the probability of an end to the conflict.
Polymarket odds on the lifting of the US naval blockade of Iran for end of March 2027 are at 71%, from 64% prior.
Possible increase in AI regulation and scrutiny is cited as the reason for the AI and neocloud selloff.

tension_points.bull_case: Midterms acted as a clearing event. VIX fell 4.5 vol, technical selling was exhausted, and rates, dollar and crude all moved in line with lower escalation risk. Polymarket odds of the naval blockade lifting by end of March 2027 rose to 71% from 64%.
tension_points.bear_case: Near-term Polymarket odds have barely repriced, and the desk's view that the US underperforms depends on the change in US/Iran assumptions proving correct.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The change in market assumptions on US/Iran proving incorrect, which would undercut the relative US underperformance call.
